title: HB762 (2020 Regular): Firearms silencers; increase penalties for the sale or possession of.

provenance.fetched_by: Open States bulk data (Mississippi) (gun-policy Stage 5, Mississippi); operative text read by a Sonnet fill agent from the official Mississippi text (Introduced; official copy, https://billstatus.ls.state.ms.us/documents/2020/html/HB/0700-0799/HB0762IN.htm)
provenance.note: As-filed text, no date; no passage vote recorded. Struck: 'misdemeanor', fine of up to $500 and up to 30 days in county jail; added: 'silence', felony, $2,000 minimum fine, $5,000 maximum, Department of Corrections custody.

operative_text: Section 1 (Miss. Code § 97-37-31): It shall be unlawful for any person, persons, corporation or manufacturing establishment, not duly authorized under federal law, to make, manufacture, sell or possess any instrument or device which, if used on firearms of any kind, will arrest, muffle or silence the report of the firearm when shot or fired. Any person violating this section shall be guilty of a felony and, upon conviction, shall be fined not less than Two Thousand Dollars ($2,000.00), but not more than Five Thousand Dollars ($5,000.00) for each violation, imprisoned in the custody of the Mississippi Department of Corrections, or both.
